title: "Convenience Store Growth Rate Hits Highest Since 2020... GS Retail Target Price Raised" [Click e-Stock] - 아시아경제
content:
"Convenience Store Growth Rate Hits Highest Since 2020... GS Retail Target Price Raised" [Click e-Stock] On August 11, Hana Securities stated that GS Retail has entered a phase of sustained profitability improvement, raising its target price from 31,000 won to 35,000 won. The investment opinion remained 'Buy'. Jongdae Park, a research analyst at Hana Securities, wrote in a report the same day, "In the second quarter of this year, GS Retail recorded consolidated revenue of 3.1751 trillion won, up 7% year-on-year, and operating profit of 107.4 billion won, up 27%, exceeding market consensus." He added, "Balanced growth and profitability enhancement in key business areas such as convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping are driving strong profit improvement." By business division, the same-store sales growth rate for convenience stores reached 7.5% compared to the same period last year, marking the highest figure since 2020. Park explained, "This was driven by an increased proportion of sales from foreign customers, expansion of Fresh Convenience Store (FCS) locations, and growth in quick commerce." He noted, "As the burden of fixed expenses eased, the operating margin for convenience stores rose to 3.0%." The supermarket segment also saw a 10% year-on-year increase in revenue, supported by greater contributions from quick commerce. Park stated, "By reducing poorly performing stores and increasing large FCS stores, which generate 50–60% higher sales than standard stores, GS Retail has enhanced store-level efficiency." He added, "Acceleration of quick commerce centered around the in-house application 'Our Neighborhood GS' is creating synergies between the convenience store and supermarket businesses, further fueling growth." © The Asia Business Daily. Per a recently released Goldman Sachs report, “Global M&A volumes rose 48% YoY against an unusually supportive backdrop,” which was “driven primarily by the surge in deal size, with mega M&A volumes +125% YoY.” And the firm expects that strength to continue, saying that the M&A cycle has “substantial room to run, despite long-standing geopolitical and inflationary pressures.” Further, we’re witnessing a historical IPO market (which is great for the underwriters), as the recently completed second quarter saw nearly $116 billion in IPO proceeds (largely driven by the SpaceX IPO), which marks the second-highest quarterly total this century, behind only the first quarter of 2021 (at $133 billion). Should dealmaking continue apace, and should we see the much-anticipated IPOs of Anthropic or OpenAI emerge, it looks like the environment should remain supportive for investment banks. With that in mind, let’s take a look at two of Wall Street’s heaviest hitters when it comes to dealmaking: Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS). MS has been the better performer over the last year, rising 49.5% compared to 43.5% for GS. But over the last five years, Goldman Sachs has handily outperformed the competition, with a 151.2% gain compared to Morgan Stanley’s 106.9% increase. That said, both stocks are trading just off their all-time highs, so if you were inclined to give the round to MS, I wouldn’t argue. While dealmaking fees are independent of an investment bank’s book of assets, P/B is still a reality check for banks. On that lens, GS looks less stretched than MS. MS offers a modestly higher dividend yield, but if your 2026 thesis includes “higher-for-longer rates plus decent equity returns,” that extra yield can be meaningful—especially if deal volumes don’t accelerate as quickly as hoped. MS is more popular among institutional investors, who hold meaningfully more of the “float” (publicly available shares) than they do in GS. But that can cut both ways, as it suggests deep sponsorship and broad index/fund participation (often supportive in drawdowns) but can also mean more “crowding” (less incremental buyer power and more selling “ammunition” if sentiment flips). Goldman Sachs is the 800-pound gorilla when it comes to investment banking and is routinely at the top of the heap when it comes to total volume. In the first half of 2026, Goldman advised on an astronomical $1.3 trillion in deals (per this scorecard from dealogic), which put them well ahead of Morgan Stanley’s $880 billion. That follows a 2025 in which Goldman was also at the front of the pack ($1.6 trillion in deals vs. Morgan Stanley’s $1.1 trillion), and a similarly weighted 2024 ($968 billion for Goldman; $744 billion for Morgan Stanley). These are both heavy hitters, but Goldman leaves the competition in the dust, and when advisory and underwriting activity rises, the bank that’s already winning the biggest mandates tends to capture a disproportionate share of the incremental fees. And that’s especially important this year, which has seen an increase in the number of large deals and a decrease in the number of smaller mergers. Both are elite, but the market exposure isn’t identical: So even if both banks continue to participate in the 2026 surge, GS gives you more exposure to the thesis. Both companies should do well in a deal-heavy environment, and they’re both “Bull Market Stocks” (as Mike Cintolo would put it), but if you’re looking to play the M&A and IPO boom in 2026, Goldman Sachs gives you the most upside. *This post has been updated to reflect current market conditions. title: VB-G RAM G’s first month shows sharp fall in rural jobs: Jairam Ramesh - The Tribune
content: "The first month of the Modi government's VB-G RAM G scheme is already bringing to light the cost of dismantling MGNREGA," Ramesh said. He said the figures vindicated concerns raised by the Congress and other Opposition parties when the government replaced MGNREGA with the new legislation. Ramesh said MGNREGA provided rural workers with a legal guarantee of employment and gave gram panchayats a central role in implementing the programme. "The core spirit of MGNREGA was to free workers from dependence on the whims and mercy of the government of the day," he said. Drawing a contrast with VB-G RAM G, Ramesh alleged that the new scheme had centralised implementation, placed a greater financial burden on state governments and made access to employment increasingly dependent on technology and biometric authentication. He further alleged that the new framework had removed the employment guarantee and made it more difficult for rural workers to claim their entitlements. Ramesh said the nearly 50 per cent decline in workdays generated under the new scheme during its first month showed the impact of the changes. "This is exactly the situation that the Congress and the entire Opposition had warned about when the Modi government bulldozed MGNREGA," he said. Calling the new scheme "outright employment theft", Ramesh alleged that the government's policy was weakening a legal safeguard that had provided rural households with access to employment during periods of economic distress. title: GS Power Partners Announces Leadership Succession - Yahoo Finance
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results NEW YORK, August 10, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--GS Power Partners is pleased to announce a strengthened leadership team to support its next phase of growth. Effective August 10, 2026, Michael D. Smith will join as President and Chief Executive Officer, with Co-Founder and current CEO Jason Kuflik transitioning to the role of Executive Chairman. Since co-founding GS Power Partners, Jason has built the company from the ground up, assembling the team, establishing the platform, securing the capital, and driving the strategy that has put the company in the strong position it is in today. In his new role, Jason will remain actively engaged with the business, specifically supporting key external relationships and contributing as a significant shareholder. His continued involvement is a strong signal of confidence in the company's direction. Michael brings more than 25 years of energy industry experience and a strong track record of scaling businesses to the role of President and Chief Executive Officer. Michael most recently served as CEO of CPower Energy, the nation's largest distributed energy resource monetization provider, with over 6 GW of capacity across nearly 20,000 customer sites. Prior to that, he served as CEO of ForeFront Power, a leading distributed solar and energy storage developer operating across the U.S. and Mexico. He has also held senior roles at Constellation and Exelon, including SVP of Distributed Energy and leadership of Constellation Technology Ventures. He brings deep industry relationships, institutional operating experience, and a clear understanding of what it takes to create value for all stakeholders. With the completion of a $250 million corporate loan facility with Deutsche Bank and a defined Value Creation Plan in place, GS Power Partners is well-positioned to execute on its pipeline and scale toward its growth objectives over the next five years. GS Power Partners is a developer, financier, owner and operator of distributed generation (DG) commercial and industrial and community solar projects across the United States. Since the company's founding in 2015, GS Power Partners has been fully focused on project development in the North American DG solar sector. The company is backed by CVC DIF, a global investment firm with almost €23 billion in assets under management. The company maintains a portfolio of 400+ megawatts of operating projects across 40+ funds and 125+ projects, mainly concentrated in the Northeast and Midwest. GS Power Partners advances the clean energy transition through responsible investments and long-term partnerships. title: LS Electric, GS E&C Partner on DC Power Distribution for AI Data Centers - thelec.net
content: LS Electric and GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) have agreed to collaborate on direct current (DC) power distribution technology and power equipment supply for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. LS Electric said on Aug. 10 that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with GS E&C to jointly respond to changes in the AI data center business environment. Under the agreement, the companies will develop next-generation DC power distribution technologies aimed at improving power efficiency in high-power, high-density AI data centers. As part of the partnership, LS Electric will supply key electrical equipment for AI data center projects being developed by GS E&C, including switchboards, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) and extra-high-voltage transformers. LS Electric is currently developing DC power distribution products such as solid-state transformers (SSTs), solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) and energy storage systems (ESS). The company has also established a production facility at its Cheonan site in South Chungcheong Province that operates entirely on a DC power distribution system. An LS Electric official said demand for DC power distribution technologies is increasing as operators seek to improve the power efficiency of AI data centers.

title: Vikings Training Camp Observations: Jamal Adams Switches Jersey & Roles - Minnesota Vikings
content: EAGAN, Minn. — An early afternoon thunderstorm preceded a gorgeous afternoon of football Friday at TCO Performance Center as the Vikings picked back up in full pads after a day off. In case you've lost track of the 2026 Training Camp action, Minnesota will be headed to New Jersey a week from now to prepare for its preseason opener at the New York Giants on Saturday, Aug. 15. As far as the ongoing quarterback competition between Kyler Murray, who turned 29 today, and J.J. McCarthy, both players made a couple difficult throws in a session heavy with specific game situations, and they had a couple more fall incomplete by the skin of their teeth. Two stuck with us: Murray laid one up the seam to TE Ben Yurosek that almost resulted in a diving catch, and McCarthy arced one up the sideline to TE Gavin Bartholomew that looked grabbable — granted, it would've been a head-turner. On the defensive side, Dallas Turner, Andrew Van Ginkel and Blake Cashman supplied some of the most notable pressure on the passers, and Jalen Redmond played with ownership of the trenches. Here are three observations from practice No. 8, which was officiated by NFL referees: View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp practice on August 7. We got our first long look this summer at All-Pro kicker Will Reichard, and he looked as advertised. During an extended period (nearly 20 minutes), the offense worked third- and fourth-down calls, and depending on the result either finished the sequence by sending out the field goal/punting units or leaving the offense on the field to convert. Ultimately, Reichard was tasked with five FG attempts. The 25-year-old drilled his initial try from 57 yards and then narrowly missed his second from 58 yards, which hit the crossbar. He responded with makes from 46, 43 and 48 yards to finish 4-for-5. As well as he performed, it's not outlandish to say rookie punter Brett Thorson stole the show. Thorson followed veteran Johnny Hekker, who punted twice (one of Hekker's was downed at the 20-yard line, the other bounced through the back of the end zone), and placed his first ball at the 1-yard line (Tai Felton gunned down the field and missed a chance to down it before it rolled into the end zone). Afterward, in a separate special teams period, Thorson took all the punter reps and compiled his own highlight reel, smashing ball after ball to smithereens. We couldn't get a perfect read on the distances but are comfortable saying several traveled 60 yards. The returners were in retreat mode. It was a fun introduction for fans to the Australian punter and the Ray Guy Award winner at Georgia. Jamal Adams sported a new number, 32, after donning 54 in his first seven Vikings practices. The 30-year-old defender probably feels a little bit more at home in it after rocking 33 on the Jets and Seahawks (and Titans and Raiders). Adams likely also felt more himself as he moved all around Minnesota's defense. Adams is listed as a linebacker on the roster and was just that to begin his Vikings tenure, playing alongside the likes of Blake Cashman, Eric Wilson and Ivan Pace, Jr. On Friday, however, Adams got more exposure to Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores' creativity and played in the box, over the slot and as one of two deep safeties next to Joshua Metellus. It's worth noting that safety Jay Ward did not practice, and rookie Jakobe Thomas did not participate in team drills. Nevertheless, it was neat to see Adams patrolling several areas.
